newsitem.title: GERMANY: Top German TV networks boost ad prices.
newsitem.headline: Top German TV networks boost ad prices.

text.p: Top German television groups ProSieben Media AG and the RTL network said on Friday they would raise advertising prices for their stations in 1998.

In their annual ad price announcements, the groups' media marketing agencies Media Gruppe Muenchen (MGM) and IP Deutschland said market conditions had created conditions for higher asking prices for television ads.
"Our price policy for 1997 has succeeded," said MGM, which is a unit of the ProSieben group, in a statement announcing the price hikes. "MGM intends to continue building on this growth."
The ProSieben Media Group will raise ad prices on its ProSieben station an average of 4.5 percent, MGM said. Its second channel Kabel 1, will have a 6.2 percent average ad price increase.
MGM said the prices applied to spots shown between 6 a.m. and 1 a.m. During prime-time, 8 p.m. and 11 p.m., prices will climb by about 4.7 percent at ProSieben and 13.9 percent at Kabel 1.
RTL's marketing agency, IP Deutschland, said the network would also be boosting prices next year.
The RTL station, Germany's largest, will have an average 5.5 percent ad price increase, RTL2 a two percent hike, and Super RTL 24 percent higher prices.

IP Deutschland said that it bases its price averages on a 24-hour day, which prevents direct comparisons with the prices given by MGM, which eliminates the hours between 1 a.m. and 6 a.m. which traditionally have the lowest viewer ratings.
During prime-time, RTL will boost prices 5.3 percent from the 1997 rate.
Media analysts use the annual price-setting to gauge the strength of individual stations and the television market as a whole.
"The growth rates in the TV advertising market continue to flatten out," said Petra Heist, an analyst at the Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich.
"This could lead to a type of price war in the non-prime-time hours," Heist said.

"However the most attractive and most expensive broadcasting time -- prime time -- continues to be almost filled to capacity," she added. "Assuming the programming is good, stations can always demand higher prices."
MGM said that the ProSieben group also expected to expand its market share, especially among the key target group of viewers under 50 years old, largely due to an improved variety of programming.

"The attractiveness of a station's programming determines ratings and advertising prices," Heist said. "ProSieben is very well positioned among the most attractive viewer group and could capture ground from RTL and (fellow private station) Sat1."
